current_date: June 2025 (requirements document headed 'Our Local Validation List Requirements (June 2025)'; companion checklist headed 'Local Validation Checklist (Revised June 2025)')
current_evidence: The official 'Submitting a planning application' page still links 'Local Validation List requirements' (PDF, 389KB) and 'Local Validation Checklist' (Local-Validation-Checklist-2025.pdf) under its Local Validation List section. The page text gives no adoption date.

issues.detail: Item 2, Local Authority Development Letter, is missing from every sheet. Trigger: all applications made under Regulation 3 of the Town and Country Planning General Regulations 1992, i.e. the County Council's own development such as schools, libraries, roads and household recycling centres. It must be a letter from the commissioning officer of the applicant department, who takes responsibility for complying with conditions.
issues.evidence: '2. Local Authority Development Letter ... All applications submitted under Regulation 3 of the 1992 Regulations.'

issues.detail: The 'County own devt (Reg 3)' sheet says '(none) No specific local requirements identified'. In fact the whole list applies to County Council (Regulation 3) development. Item 2 is Reg 3-only, and item 16 calls for a comprehensive lighting assessment for Reg 3 floodlit sports pitches. The sheet should carry all 22 items.
issues.evidence: Purpose: 'information that must be submitted ... with a planning application (for waste or County Council development)'

issues.detail: Item 5, Statement of sustainable design and construction, is missing entirely. Trigger: in South Cambridgeshire, all applications; in all other districts and Cambridge City, new schools and all developments creating more than 1,000 sq m of floorspace. The statement is needed in every district except Cambridge City. It must address climate change, and new buildings are expected to reach BREEAM Very Good overall with Excellent credits for Energy and Water.
issues.evidence: '5. Statement of sustainable design and construction ... For new schools and all developments creating more than 1,000m² of floor space.'

issues.detail: Item 21, Information in support of applications for the storage, treatment or disposal of waste, is the core waste item and is not recorded as a requirement on any sheet. Only fragments of 21(i)/(ii) leak into the s73 'site levels' and 'Health Impact Assessment' excerpts. Triggers: (1) new landfill sites or extensions to them, including land raising. These need a topographical survey, phasing plans and cross-sections, pre- and post-settlement contours, gas and leachate control, dry weather flows, soil handling, restoration, after-use and aftercare. (2) Storage, treatment or disposal of hazardous waste, and incineration (including advanced thermal) or chemical treatment of non-hazardous waste. These need a Health Impact Assessment. Both types need: waste type and source, plans and elevations, working hours, access including wheel cleaning, and surface water drainage.
issues.evidence: '21. Information in support of applications for the storage, treatment, or disposal of waste ... 1) New landfill sites or extensions ... 2) Proposals involving ... hazardous waste ... incineration'

issues.detail: Item 11, Landscape and biodiversity enhancement management scheme, is not captured. Its aftercare text is filed under an invented 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage details' row. Trigger: where soft landscape or biodiversity enhancement measures are proposed (items 4 and 10), and for new landfill sites or their extension (aftercare of restored land). Content: a management programme of at least 5 years, and restoration, after-use and aftercare for temporary waste proposals, possibly 10+ years.
issues.evidence: '11. Landscape and biodiversity enhancement management scheme ... Applications for new landfill sites or their extension will require aftercare'

issues.detail: Two district-specific sub-items of item 5 are missing. 5(i): a completed Cambridge City Sustainable Development Checklist (Section 4 of the Sustainable Design and Construction SPD), required within Cambridge City only. 5(ii): a Water Conservation Strategy, required within South Cambridgeshire for all non-residential development unless shown not practicable (e.g. operational buildings with no water supply or welfare facilities).
issues.evidence: Checklist item 5 '(i) Cambridge City Completed Sustainable Development Checklist (Within Cambridge City only)'; '(ii) Water Conservation Strategy (Within South Cambridgeshire only)'

issues.detail: Item 17's waste-related schemes are missing. A Dust Management Scheme is needed where dust is likely to be an issue. A bioaerosols risk assessment is needed for open-air composting facilities within 250m of a residential property. Grokbot's 'Odour / Dust / Vibration assessment' row actually quotes noise text, and the Odour Management Scheme appears only under a mislabelled 'Ventilation / Extraction details' row.
issues.evidence: 'A bioaerosols risk assessment is required for open air composting facilities within 250m of a residential property.'

issues.detail: Item 1(i), a public art statement within the Planning Statement, is missing. Trigger: within South Cambridgeshire, developments proposing 1,000 sq m or more of new floorspace.
issues.evidence: '(i) Consideration of Public Art for developments of 1,000 square metres and above (South Cambridgeshire District Council only)'

issues.detail: The Low Emissions Strategy sub-items are not recorded as requirements; they appear only as stray text inside other rows. 12(i): a Low Emissions Strategy Statement, needed in South Cambridgeshire (and Huntingdonshire, per the checklist) wherever a Transport Assessment/Statement or Travel Plan is required, justifying parking and EV charging. 17(i): a low emissions strategy, needed in Huntingdonshire when the air quality assessment shows significant effects.
issues.evidence: Checklist 12 '(i) Within South Cambridgeshire and Huntingdonshire only, a Low Emissions Strategy Statement'; 17 '(i) Within Huntingdonshire only'

issues.detail: Huntingdonshire-only parking details under item 13 are missing. Proposals with car and cycle parking must justify vehicle space, parking levels and plug-in/low-emission charging. New non-residential buildings over 2,500 sq m net internal floorspace must consider dedicated changing and showering facilities for cyclists.
issues.evidence: Item 13: 'within Huntingdonshire District Councils area proposals for new non-residential buildings over 2,500 square metres ... changing and showering facilities for cyclists'

issues.detail: The checklist says the same 22-item list applies to every planning application, including s73 and s73A. Grokbot instead treats the checklist as an s73-specific list and splits the items unevenly between two sheets. Full planning lacks LVIA (9), CEMP/Traffic Management Plan (13A), Open Space/Playing Field (20), Noise (15, filed only under Minerals & waste), Lighting (16, filed under Listed building consent and as 'Advertisement drawings'), Highways/access (13), Local Authority Development Letter (2), sustainable design (5) and waste information (21). The s73 sheet lacks Travel Plan (14), Noise (15), the landscape and biodiversity management scheme (11), sustainable design (5), the Local Authority Development Letter (2) and waste information (21).
issues.evidence: 'This Local Validation Checklist applies to all applications for planning permission ... (including those made under Section 73 ... AND SECTION 73A)'

issues.detail: Some rows are filed under application types the list does not cover. 'Lighting Assessment / External lighting scheme' is filed under Listed building consent only because 'a listed building' is one of its location triggers. The County list does not cover listed building consent. 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' is filed under Outline from a biodiversity guidance-note fragment. The list says EIA falls under separate regulations outside its scope, and it names no Outline-specific items.
issues.evidence: NOTES: 'Environmental Impact Assessment development is covered by separate regulations, which are mainly outside of the scope of these guidance notes.'

issues.detail: The 'Minerals & waste (county)' sheet mixes up scope. The list does not apply to mineral development at all, yet most rows come from a separate Mineral and Waste Policy Guidance Checklist (not part of the validation list, and not in the upload). They cover mineral-only policy items such as Mineral Safeguarding Areas, borrowpits and aerodrome safeguarding. Meanwhile waste applications, which the list does cover, get only the noise item. The waste-specific triggers are not filed there: item 21, the 7A drainage trigger 'Waste planning applications', 17 waste emissions to air, 11 landfill aftercare and 19 waste audit.
issues.evidence: 'neither the Standard Planning Application Form nor the Local Validation List currently applies to applications for mineral development'

issues.detail: Many Full planning excerpts quote information-required text or a different item's text instead of the trigger. Transport Assessment and Travel Plan both quote the South Cambridgeshire low-emissions sentence. The real triggers: a TA where there are significant transport implications, including new schools; a TS where there are some implications; a Travel Plan where vehicle movements rise significantly, or a school gains one or more classrooms (30 pupils) or a pre-school. Drainage Strategy/SuDS quotes foul drainage text; the real trigger is major development, 1,000 sq m+ floorspace, sites of 1 ha+ in any flood zone, or waste applications. Tree survey quotes the 2014 biodiversity guidance notes; the real trigger is trees or hedges on or next to the site that could be affected. Parking provision quotes the red-line rule from item 22. Planning Statement should read 'All, except very minor developments with no policy implications'. SCI should read 'Category A development' (SCI January 2019). Waste audit should read: demolition, possibly contaminated brownfield land, or significant earthmoving.
issues.evidence: Item 12 'Transport Assessment – where the proposed development has significant transport implications including new schools'; item 14 'net increase of one or more classrooms'

issues.detail: Several triggers are cut off or garbled. BNG: 'except for BNG exempt developments.' should read 'Required for all applications except for BNG exempt developments', and the watercourse metric is needed within 10m of watercourses. Landscaping: 'mitigated by landscape planting. 17 Information required' includes a page number; the trigger is tree or hedgerow removal needing compensatory planting, or a visual impact that planting could mitigate. Site levels: 'Plans and Drawings ... Policy Driver' should be sloping sites and all applications with level changes. Contaminated land: 'Link to the Environment Agency ... 29 Management Advice' should be contamination known or suspected, a site near contaminated land, or a vulnerable use such as schools or care homes. HIA stops at 'Within Huntingdonshire District Council's area:' and drops the Huntingdonshire 2,500 sq m/2 ha (rapid) and 10,000 sq m (full) thresholds and the Fenland major-development trigger. FRA quotes only the Flood Zone 2/3 clause and drops the Flood Zone 1 triggers (over 1 ha; under 1 ha with other flood sources, a more vulnerable use, hardstanding changes, SFRA future-risk areas or critical drainage problems). The Lighting trigger ends at 'conservation area, 26'.
issues.evidence: Full planning and Listed building consent rows in app_type_rows

issues.detail: District-only sub-requirements are given as the main trigger. Air Quality quotes only the extra Huntingdonshire trigger (10,000 sq m or 2 ha). It omits the county-wide triggers: within or next to an AQMA; risk of AQMA designation or significant worsening; conflict with an air quality action plan; or a waste proposal with emissions to air, including dust, odour and bioaerosols. EV charging quotes South Cambridgeshire policy TI/3, and HIA applies only in South Cambridgeshire, Huntingdonshire and Fenland. This is the County's own list (not a joint list), but these sub-items apply only to sites in the named districts.
issues.evidence: Item 17: 'Is a waste proposal where there will be emissions to air, including dust, odour and bioaerosols.' / 'Within Huntingdonshire District Council's area Air Quality Assessments are also required'

issues.detail: The s73 excerpts are bare checklist headings with the next item's number glued on, so they state no trigger and misnumber the item. Examples: 'Air quality assessment 18.' (item 17), 'Flood Risk Assessment 7A.' (item 7), 'Heritage Statement 1 9.' (item 8 plus a page number) and 'Planning Statement' as 'within the planning statement; and not relevant for each of the following items: 1.'. The 'site levels' and 'Health Impact Assessment' rows share one fragment of item 21(i)/(ii).
issues.evidence: Checklist index '7. Flood Risk Assessment / 7A. Surface water drainage strategy ... / 17. Air quality assessment / 18. Contaminated land assessment'

issues.detail: Several rows use requirement names that do not exist in the list, attached to text from a different item. 'Advertisement drawings / illumination details' is the item 16 lighting assessment (isolux text). 'Habitats Regulations Assessment / SPA mitigation' is the item 7A dry weather flows assessment. 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage details' is the item 11 waste-site aftercare text. 'Ventilation / Extraction details (odour)' is the item 17 Odour Management Scheme. 'Ecological Survey / Assessment' quotes the Huntingdonshire low-emissions clause. 'Minerals / Waste specific statements' is the item 19 Waste Audit, which applies to any development with demolition or earthmoving, not only to minerals or waste applications.
issues.evidence: Item 7A 'Dry Weather Flows An appropriate assessment of dry weather flows is needed'; item 16 'An isolux contour map ... vertical illuminance and showing neighbouring buildings'

issues.detail: Of the 11 tab_items, only the scale-bar drawing standard is a requirement. The rest are the redaction notice, the pre-application guide file-size/fee text, 'Failure to consider all necessary points will mean that the application will be invalid', 'An invalid application cannot be registered...', 'This checklist should be read together with the national validation requirements', and bare 2014 biodiversity checklist fragments such as 'Special Protection Areas (SPA),' and 'Ouse Washes SAC, SPA and Ramsar site).'. None of the 22 numbered list items appear in tab_items. The 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' rows (Full, s73, Minerals & waste) are also not requirements: the list only encourages pre-application advice.
issues.evidence: 'Applicants are encouraged to take advantage of the pre-application services that we offer'

issues.detail: Several requirements are split across two rows. Drainage Strategy/SuDS and Foul Sewage share the s73 excerpt 'Surface water drainage strategy and foul drainage strategy 8.' (one combined item, 7A). Transport Assessment and Travel Plan share the same Full planning sentence. The s73 'site levels' and 'Health Impact Assessment' rows share an identical excerpt. 'Biodiversity Checklist' and 'Ecological Survey' both stand for item 4.
issues.evidence: '7A. Surface water drainage strategy and foul drainage strategy'

issues.detail: The list date 2025-08-01 comes from PDF CreationDate metadata. Both documents state June 2025 (the requirements guidance is dated June 2025; the checklist is 'Revised June 2025'), so the list date should be June 2025. Either date is under 2 years old, so the 'Outdated (>2y)? No' flag is still correct. The document also commits to review at least every 2 years.
issues.evidence: 'Our Local Validation List Requirements (June 2025)'; 'LOCAL VALIDATION CHECKLIST (Revised June 2025)'

summary: Grokbot linked the correct, current list: the County's June 2025 Local Validation List Requirements, with its June 2025 checklist. But it took the date from PDF metadata (August 2025), and the extraction is poor. It misses the Local Authority Development Letter, the sustainable design and construction statement and the waste storage/treatment/disposal information outright, and leaves the County own development (Reg 3) sheet empty. It spreads the 22 items unevenly between Full planning and s73, under several invented labels, with most triggers cut off or copied from other items. A re-extraction should apply all 22 items to every waste and County Council planning application (including s73/s73A) and exclude minerals.
